items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Uh, was, uh, Mike Fritzel, the, uh, boss, uh? Yeah, that's right, that's right.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's right. B. Palmer, and it was Santo Picora, who is now at the, uh, famous door. Emmett Hardy on trumpet, there was the trumpet boy. Uh, Leona Paula, Frisco on drums, no, Martin Burke on drums, and, uh, Al Siegel on piano. And she had a shimmy act that went out in vaudeville, and it was a wonderful act. And, uh, then Rap, uh, that, that thing broke up. It lasted a pretty good long time, a couple of years on the off-room circuit. And then Rap left, and that's when we, when we got him in, uh, Davenport.…
Uh, was, uh, Mike Fritzel, the, uh, boss, uh? Yeah, that's right, that's right. You don't have to lean over close to the dingus. No. You don't have to talk right at that, that'll take a moment.

We replaced, uh, Frank Snyder with Ben Pollack, and we replaced Elmer Schoble with Mel Stitzel on piano, then we replaced Arnold Lake Canna with Steve Brown, who to me was the world's greatest jazz bass player. In fact, he started all these guys slapping a bass. No. And I think he's now Secretary of the Union in Detroit.
